newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Elton John lets sun go down on HK handover concert.
newsitem.headline: Elton John lets sun go down on HK handover concert.

text.p: British singer Elton John has pulled the plug on plans to mark the handover of Hong Kong with a rock concert extravaganza after local politicians objected to the noise.
A statement from John's managers received by Reuters on Friday said the concerts would not go ahead because of the noise controversy.
Local authorities in Hong Kong said they would refuse to waive stringent noise restrictions at the territory's main stadium for John's two planned concerts.
"The waiver was instrumental to negotiations and, there being no suitable alternative venues, it will therefore be impossible to stage the concerts," the statement said.
Local politicians earlier suggested the fans could wear earphones to get around the restrictions -- an idea widely ridiculed in Hong Kong.

"The city with noise pollution that shatters the nerves of citizens on 364 days of the year is now going to turn a pop concert on the 365th into a mime act during celebrations of one of its most historic events of the century," scoffed the South China Morning Post newspaper.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over 150 years, reverts to China at the stroke of midnight on June 30, 1997.
The handover is expected to be marked with a massive fireworks show over Hong Kong harbour which organisers have boasted will be the world's greatest pyrotechnic display.
The spokesman for Governor Chris Patten said John had been offered two alternative sites but turned them down because they were unsuitable for the spectacular effects he had in mind.
"People overseas will be puzzled by what they will see as a daft decision by legislators," spokesman Kerry McGlynn said.
